A glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip at idle under electrical load.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

messages.content: At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. Our family's 2015 midsize sedan with the 2.5L, just past 110,624 miles. I have one afternoon off, so tell me the part and I'll knock it out.

snippets.title: Warm air from rear AC only
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. The front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm because the rear expansion valve sticks closed. Compare front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. Repair: replace the rear expansion valve.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2011-2018. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

messages.content: The AC isn't cooling anymore. Air from all the front vents, both sides, is barely cooler than outside, from the moment I start it. Fan speeds all work. Mine is a hatchback from 2014, 1.6-liter four under the hood, 166k miles so far. Which check would you run before anything else?

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from slipping fan clutch
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. Temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic if the viscous fan clutch slips. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. Repair: replace the fan clutch.

snippets.title: Radiator temperature drop check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical. A much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow through the radiator.

snippets.title: Electric radiator fan operation check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with electric radiator fans (2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines; not the 5.5L V8). With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. A fan that does not run lets coolant temperature climb in traffic while highway airflow keeps it normal at speed.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

messages.content: Got a 2013 midsize sedan here, 2.5L four-cylinder, around 47,981 miles on it. The temperature gauge climbs toward hot when I'm sitting in traffic or at a long light, and it drops back to normal as soon as I'm moving at highway speed. Any idea which check to begin with?
Good details, thanks. The first check is this: with the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line [SM-9926].
I don't love the idea of testing stuff. Can we just go with the head gasket?
A part guess could cost you twice. With the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line [SM-9926].
Grudgingly did the test. Level is at the cold-fill line, nothing low.
That result clears it. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts [SM 2.2.8].
Commanded the fan with my scanner and it spun up on both speeds. Where should I go with this from here?

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: Alternator AC ripple test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Higher ripple indicates a failed diode in the alternator rectifier, which reduces output and can cause lights to flicker.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

messages.content: Our family's 2016 hatchback with the 1.6L four-cylinder, just past 125k miles. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. Normal there. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy loads on, measure voltage drop between the alternator output terminal and the battery positive post [SM-4573].

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2011-2018. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

messages.content: The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Our family's 2017 compact crossover with the 2.4L four-cylinder, just past 151,883 miles. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Low state of charge on short trips with auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. Vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes may show a low battery message because the battery monitoring sensor limits charging. Check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. Repair: update the body control software and reset the sensor.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Repair: update the head unit software.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

messages.content: If the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. Mine is a midsize SUV from 2015, 3.4-liter V6 under the hood, 26k miles so far.

snippets.title: Strut upper mount check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front struts. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

messages.content: The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. This is my 2015 compact crossover. It has the 2.4L and about 189,574 miles. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Clicking or clunk at full steering lock
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, may come from a worn outer CV joint. Inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. Repair: replace the axle shaft.

snippets.title: Parasitic draw test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. A higher draw indicates a circuit that stays awake.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2012 midsize SUV, 3.4L V6, odometer 122k. The front left side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Every video I watched blames the ball joint. Agree, yes?

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Parasitic draw test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. A higher draw indicates a circuit that stays awake.

messages.content: Mine is a minivan from 2017, 3.5L V6 under the hood, 67k miles so far. If the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from slipping fan clutch
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. Temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic if the viscous fan clutch slips. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. Repair: replace the fan clutch.

snippets.title: Pressure cap test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. A cap that vents early lets coolant escape through the overflow as vapor, which can lower the level with no visible leak or puddle.

snippets.title: Pedal pulsation at low speed on rough roads from ABS activation
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. A pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound may occur during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement because of early ABS activation. Inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. Repair: replace the affected hub and tone ring.

snippets.title: Residual fuel pressure after hot shutdown
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Drive until the engine is at full operating temperature, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and record the pressure 20 minutes later. Pressure should stay above 30 psi. A faster drop lets fuel boil in the hot rail, which shows up as a long crank on restarts after a short stop.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

messages.content: This is my 2014 compact crossover. It has the 2.4L four-cylinder and about 31k miles. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: CVT judder on light acceleration
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. A judder or shudder may be felt during light acceleration from 15-35 mph. Check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Repair: replace the CVT fluid and update the control software.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

messages.content: The automatic slams into second, a hard 1-2 shift, and it's worse once the transmission is fully warmed up. Daily driver is a 2015 compact sedan (2.0L) with 107k miles. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. Slow coolant loss may come from a seeping turbocharger coolant return line fitting. Inspect the fitting and the line for dried coolant residue with the engine cold. Repair: replace the coolant line and sealing washers.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket

snippets.title: Rotor lateral runout measurement
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

messages.content: Hi. 2012 compact sedan, 2.0L four-cylinder engine, roughly 35k on the odometer. I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. What's a sensible first test here?

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

snippets.title: Spark plug inspection and gap check
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in) and look for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking down the porcelain, or oil or fuel fouling.

messages.content: I bought a used 2018 midsize sedan with the 2.5-liter four; it shows 38,426 miles. It bucks under load, like merging onto the highway, and the scan tool shows P0303. No problem at idle, rain or shine. Any idea which check to begin with?
Begin here: pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SEC 8.22].
Do I really have to test it? I'd rather just buy the spark plug.

Ordering parts without a test risks money on the wrong one. Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [SEC 8.22].
Went out and checked it like you said. The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain.
Normal there. Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SM 4.6.3].
The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it. Nothing showed up, so I'm guessing it's the spark plug. Agree?

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Lean code under boost from loose charge air pipe
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. P0171 may set during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal. Inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. Repair: reseat the pipe and install a new clamp.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

messages.content: Shop ticket: 2015 full-size pickup, 5.5L V8, odometer 71k. CEL came on with P0171. It idles rough at stoplights and stumbles a little right after a cold start, but it pulls fine on the highway. Save me the troubleshooting and name whatever is worn out.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Hot restart delay from fuel pump relay contacts
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. After towing or extended idling in hot weather, worn contacts in the fuel pump relay can delay fuel pump prime on restart. Check the relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Repair: replace the fuel pump relay.

messages.content: I bought a used 2013 hatchback with the 1.6L; it shows 31k miles. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine. What should I test to start narrowing it down?

snippets.title: Lean code under boost from loose charge air pipe
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2021. P0171 may set during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal. Inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. Repair: reseat the pipe and install a new clamp.

snippets.title: Strut upper mount check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front struts. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing.

messages.content: There's a clunk from the front right when I go over speed bumps or potholes at low speed, driving straight. Nothing when I turn the wheel in a parking lot. Mine is a full-size pickup from 2013, 5.5-liter V8 under the hood, 98,395 miles so far. My neighbor fixed his by putting in a new control arm. Same deal for me, right?

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Electric radiator fan operation check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with electric radiator fans (2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines; not the 5.5L V8). With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. A fan that does not run lets coolant temperature climb in traffic while highway airflow keeps it normal at speed.

messages.content: Our family's 2018 compact sedan with the 2.0L four-cylinder, just past 41,954 miles. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. One more thing: hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Hot restart delay from fuel pump relay contacts
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. After towing or extended idling in hot weather, worn contacts in the fuel pump relay can delay fuel pump prime on restart. Check the relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Repair: replace the fuel pump relay.

messages.content: Got a 2010 compact sedan here, 1.8L four-cylinder, around 180k miles on it. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Parasitic draw test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. A higher draw indicates a circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Battery lamp at cold startup with belt squeal
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. Below 10 deg F, the battery warning lamp may light for the first minute after a cold start with a short belt squeal, and it clears once the engine warms. Inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. Repair: install the revised tensioner.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2015 midsize sedan, 3.5L V6, 152k miles logged. The battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: CVT judder on light acceleration
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. A judder or shudder may be felt during light acceleration from 15-35 mph. Check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Repair: replace the CVT fluid and update the control software.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side.

snippets.title: Battery lamp at cold startup with belt squeal
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. Below 10 deg F, the battery warning lamp may light for the first minute after a cold start with a short belt squeal, and it clears once the engine warms. Inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. Repair: install the revised tensioner.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2019 hatchback (1.6L) with 27k miles. The battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. Save me the troubleshooting and name whatever is worn out.

snippets.title: Electric radiator fan operation check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with electric radiator fans (2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines; not the 5.5L V8). A fan that does not run lets coolant temperature climb in traffic while highway airflow keeps it normal at speed.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Radiator temperature drop check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical. A much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow through the radiator.

messages.content: This is my 2010 minivan. It has the 3.5L V6 and about 151,386 miles. The temperature gauge climbs toward hot when I'm sitting in traffic or at a long light, and it drops back to normal as soon as I'm moving at highway speed. What's a sensible first test here?
With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts [SEC 8.17]. Let me know what you find.
Seems like overkill. Everyone online says water pump.
A part guess could cost you twice. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts [SEC 8.17].
Went out and checked it like you said. Turned the AC on and the radiator fan kicked on right away.
Thanks for checking. With the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line [SEC 5.8].
Level is at the cold-fill line, nothing low. Which test makes sense now that this one came back fine?

snippets.title: Parasitic draw test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. A higher draw indicates a circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

messages.content: Our family's 2017 minivan with the 3.5-liter V6, just past 74k miles. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving.

snippets.title: Clicking or clunk at full steering lock
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, may come from a worn outer CV joint. Inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. Repair: replace the axle shaft.

snippets.title: Pedal pulsation at low speed on rough roads from ABS activation
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. A pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound may occur during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement because of early ABS activation. Inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. Repair: replace the affected hub and tone ring.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

messages.content: Please keep it simple and just name the bad part. Mine is a compact crossover from 2015, 2.4L under the hood, 142k miles so far. The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Just confirm the sway bar link is shot and I'll stop bugging you.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Rotor lateral runout measurement
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

snippets.title: No-start in extreme cold
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. In temperatures below 0 deg F, a battery that is healthy in mild weather may not crank the engine after sitting overnight, with no parasitic draw present. Check the battery temperature rating and whether a block heater is fitted and used. Repair: install a higher CCA battery or a battery warmer.

messages.content: Mine is a midsize sedan from 2011, 3.5-liter V6 under the hood, 106k miles so far. If the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. What test makes sense right now?

snippets.title: Low state of charge on short trips with auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. Vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes may show a low battery message because the battery monitoring sensor limits charging. Check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. Repair: update the body control software and reset the sensor.

snippets.title: Battery lamp at cold startup with belt squeal
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. Below 10 deg F, the battery warning lamp may light for the first minute after a cold start with a short belt squeal, and it clears once the engine warms. Inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. Repair: install the revised tensioner.

snippets.title: Strut upper mount check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front struts. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing.

messages.content: This is my 2012 hatchback. It has the 1.6L four-cylinder and about 137k miles. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. Skip the explanation. Is the starter the thing to buy?

snippets.title: Residual fuel pressure after hot shutdown
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Drive until the engine is at full operating temperature, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and record the pressure 20 minutes later. Pressure should stay above 30 psi. A faster drop lets fuel boil in the hot rail, which shows up as a long crank on restarts after a short stop.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

messages.content: Our family's 2020 compact crossover with the 2.4-liter four, just past 178,132 miles. When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Accessory drive belt and tensioner inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. With the engine off, inspect the accessory drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. A glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip at idle under electrical load.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Alternator AC ripple test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Higher ripple indicates a failed diode in the alternator rectifier, which reduces output and can cause lights to flicker.

messages.content: Mine is a minivan from 2013, 3.5L V6 under the hood, 38,535 miles so far. The battery light comes on now and then at idle with the lights and blower on, and the headlights look dim. Revving it makes the light go out. Outside temperature doesn't matter. What's a sensible first test here?

Good details, thanks. The first check is this: with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SEC 5.4].
Do I really have to test it? I'd rather just buy the battery.

Ordering parts without a test risks money on the wrong one. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SEC 5.4].
Alright, I gave it a shot. 14.1 volts at the battery with everything on.
Normal there. With the engine off, inspect the accessory belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs and confirm the tensioner indicator is within its marked range [SM 5.2.7].
Belt and tensioner both look fine, no cracks. Nothing showed up, so I'm guessing it's the battery. Agree?

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Mass airflow sensor reading at idle
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). A reading well below that while long-term fuel trim is high suggests the sensor is under-reporting airflow.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to all models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

messages.content: The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. The blower works on all speeds. Mine is a compact crossover from 2015, 2.4L under the hood, 117,220 miles so far. Which check would you run before anything else?

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from slipping fan clutch
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines with an engine-driven fan, model years 2013-2020. Temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic if the viscous fan clutch slips. With the engine off and cool, spin the fan by hand: it should turn no more than about one revolution. Repair: replace the fan clutch.

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature

And while I'm at it, I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself.

snippets.title: Pedal pulsation at low speed on rough roads from ABS activation
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. A pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound may occur during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement because of early ABS activation. Inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. Repair: replace the affected hub and tone ring.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Pressure cap test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. A cap that vents early lets coolant escape through the overflow as vapor, which can lower the level with no visible leak or puddle.

snippets.title: Lean code under boost from loose charge air pipe

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage

Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine

snippets.title: No-start in extreme cold
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. In temperatures below 0 deg F, a battery that is healthy in mild weather may not crank the engine after sitting overnight, with no parasitic draw present. snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Low state of charge on short trips with auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. Repair: update the body control software and reset the sensor.

messages.content: Got a 2019 full-size pickup here, 5.5L V8, around 123,222 miles on it. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. Which check would you run before anything else?

snippets.title: Coolant seepage at turbocharger coolant line

snippets.title: CVT judder on light acceleration
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. A judder or shudder may be felt during light acceleration from 15-35 mph. Check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Repair: replace the CVT fluid and update the control software.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Low state of charge on short trips with auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

snippets.title: Warm air from rear AC only

snippets.title: Spark plug inspection and gap check
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Remove the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with a plug from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in) and look for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking down the porcelain, or oil or fuel fouling.

snippets.title: Parasitic draw test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Close the doors, latch the hood switch closed and let the modules go to sleep, which can take up to 45 minutes. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. A higher draw indicates a circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

messages.content: Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. This is my 2018 hatchback. It has the 1.6-liter four and about 80k miles.

snippets.title: Electric radiator fan operation check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with electric radiator fans (2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines; not the 5.5L V8). With the engine at operating temperature and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. A fan that does not run lets coolant temperature climb in traffic while highway airflow keeps it normal at speed.

snippets.title: Misfire at idle from intake manifold runner gasket leak
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. A single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm may come from a leaking intake manifold runner gasket. With the engine idling, listen for a vacuum leak at each runner and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Strut upper mount check

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2013-2019. snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked.

messages.content: This is my 2013 midsize SUV. It has the 3.4-liter V6 and about 145,915 miles. If the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. Which check would you run before anything else?
After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SEC 18.19]. Let me know what you find.
Seems like overkill. Everyone online says starter.

Ordering parts without a test risks money on the wrong one. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SEC 18.19].
Went out and checked it like you said. After the drive it showed 14.2 V at the battery with the lights and blower on.
Normal there. Fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label [SM-3939].
Resting voltage was 12.7 and it passed the load test. I've run out of patience with testing. Which part do I order?

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Battery lamp at cold startup with belt squeal
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. Below 10 deg F, the battery warning lamp may light for the first minute after a cold start with a short belt squeal, and it clears once the engine warms. Inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. Repair: install the revised tensioner.

messages.content: Daily driver is a 2014 midsize sedan (3.5L V6) with 167k miles. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Alternator AC ripple test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Higher ripple indicates a failed diode in the alternator rectifier, which reduces output and can cause lights to flicker.

messages.content: Got a 2017 full-size pickup here, 5.5L V8, around 161k miles on it. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. Second issue. The check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0304 (cylinder 4 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Coolant seepage at turbocharger coolant line
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. Slow coolant loss may come from a seeping turbocharger coolant return line fitting. Inspect the fitting and the line for dried coolant residue with the engine cold. Repair: replace the coolant line and sealing washers.

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups, model years 2013-2020. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

messages.content: Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. I bought a used 2010 minivan with the 3.5L V6; it shows 120k miles. Any idea which check to begin with?

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes, model years 2012-2015. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points. Repair: replace the rear drums.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Clicking or clunk at full steering lock
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. A clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, may come from a worn outer CV joint. Inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. Repair: replace the axle shaft.

messages.content: The brake pedal pulses and the steering wheel shakes when I brake from highway speed on dry pavement. It's smooth when I'm not braking. Mine is a midsize SUV from 2016, 3.4L V6 under the hood, 173k miles so far. I'd like to diagnose it properly. Where's a good starting point?

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.title: Clear-flood crank test for hot restart concerns
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. If it cranks just as long, excess fuel is unlikely and fuel supply or spark should be examined.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

messages.content: When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. Got a 2016 full-size pickup here, 5.5L V8, around 78k miles on it. How would you approach this first?

snippets.title: Misfire at idle from intake manifold runner gasket leak
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. A single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm may come from a leaking intake manifold runner gasket. With the engine idling, listen for a vacuum leak at each runner and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

messages.content: Our family's 2010 minivan with the 3.5-liter V6, just past 108,903 miles. I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. Which check would you run before anything else?

snippets.title: Rotor lateral runout measurement
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the steering knuckle and set the plunger about 0.5 in from the outer edge of the rotor face. Rotate the rotor one full turn. Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front disc brakes. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed.

messages.content: Hi. 2016 compact sedan, 1.8-liter engine engine, roughly 49k on the odometer. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. snippets.title: Accessory drive belt and tensioner inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. With the engine off, inspect the accessory drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. A glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip at idle under electrical load.

snippets.title: Cranking compression test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

messages.content: Fleet unit: 2013 minivan, 3.5L V6, 150k miles logged. It bucks under load, like merging onto the highway, and the scan tool shows P0302. No problem at idle, rain or shine. Can you point me to a good starting check?

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a front stabilizer bar. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link.

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Clear-flood crank test for hot restart concerns
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. If it cranks just as long, excess fuel is unlikely and fuel supply or spark should be examined.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side.

messages.content: It starts right up cold, but if I shut it off warm and come back 20 minutes later it cranks a long time before starting. The starter spins at its usual speed. Our family's 2016 midsize sedan with the 2.5-liter four, just past 122k miles. Quote me the repair. I'm not paying anyone to poke around.

snippets.title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
snippets.text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2022-2024. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2013-2019. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC, model years 2010-2018. The front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm because the rear expansion valve sticks closed. Compare front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. Repair: replace the rear expansion valve.

snippets.title: Strut upper mount check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with front struts. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing.

snippets.title: Pressure cap test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Fit the radiator or reservoir cap to a cap adapter on the pressure tester and pump until the cap vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. A cap that vents early lets coolant escape through the overflow as vapor, which can lower the level with no visible leak or puddle.

snippets.text: Applies to 3.5L V6, 3.4L V6 and 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2011-2021. snippets.title: Mass airflow sensor reading at idle
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor. With the engine at operating temperature and idling with all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement (about 2-2.5 g/s for a 2.0L engine). A reading well below that while long-term fuel trim is high suggests the sensor is under-reporting airflow.

snippets.title: Hot restart delay from fuel pump relay contacts
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. After towing or extended idling in hot weather, worn contacts in the fuel pump relay can delay fuel pump prime on restart. Check the relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Repair: replace the fuel pump relay.

Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.
